$ leads --help
--- stdout
usage: leads [-h]
             {kit,diagnose,candidates,log,next,sent,channel,replies,due,recheck,today,brief,cadence,strength,show,week,pipeline,preview,batch,doctor} ...

leads — the restaurant pipeline by text. ROADMAP B18 (the Saturday kit),
B25 (the remote lane), B7 (the pipeline: log, follow-ups, the week).

  leads log "Whistle Wok" talked "owner Mike, wants to see the demo" --who Mike --next fri
                               # one conversation; prints tomorrow's list back
      outcomes: held messaged visited talked inbound interested demo later trial won lost churned
      (held: not messaged, kept on file with a note — researching, or a weak fit)
      (inbound is the relay's lane: they came to us — the site form, the demo line, a reply)
      (each sets the stage and a default follow-up; --next overrides: tomorrow, fri, 3d, 2w, oct 3, none)
      (messaged needs --channel facebook|instagram|email|text|call|form: where it went, so the
       second touch knows where the first did; talked takes it too. B116)
  leads sent 1 3 4             # those picks from today's remote kit / prep outline went out (or: sent all);
                               # each gets the channel its kit planned (channel_by "kit"); --channel X overrides
  leads channel "Max Pro" facebook --date 2026-10-02 --by cowork
                               # backfill: the channel of a messaged/talked line logged without one (B116)
  leads replies "Max Pro" 7/10 --newest 2026-09-20 --by cowork --evidence URL
                               # how often the owner answers Google reviews, as a person read it (B116);
                               # `brief` prints it. Places carries no owner replies, so nothing else can.
  leads next [fri]             # the day's list (default tomorrow): follow-ups due, then new leads
  leads due                    # follow-ups due today (the 8am report)
  leads show "Whistle Wok"     # one lead's history
  leads week [--ago 1]         # this week's numbers
  leads week --by channel      # the Sunday review (B52): the funnel per channel + GROWTH § 2.4's rows
  leads pipeline [--all]       # every lead by stage
  leads pipeline --json        # counts by stage + due today, no names (B102: the owner's overview)
  leads week --json            # this week's counts as one object (B102); `--by channel --json` is the B52 envelope
  leads pipeline --strong      # only the strong ones, each with why (B73)
  leads strength "Name"        # strong / good / weak and the reasons, in words (B73)
  leads strength "Name" strong "owner asked for a call in November"
                               # Taylor's word: always wins, survives every re-score; `auto` hands it back
  leads week --by strength     # outcomes by strength and by reason, and the strong, silent (B73)

  leads today                  # the 07:30 message (B48): today's six, each with the DM to paste (or
                               # the call and what to say, B62), yesterday's replies, the follow-ups due,
                               # the first call, and the `go` words only when the email lane can send
  leads brief "Mike's Pool Care"   # one screen before the call: the fault, the preview, the history,
                               # the segment's objection and its answer, the close, the booking link
  leads cadence [--dry-run]    # the touches a silent lead is owed (GROWTH § 5.5), by its strength (B73):
                               # weak 3/10 then the pool at 30; good 3/10/30, the pool at 90; strong
                               # 3/10/30/45/60 (a call)/90, never the pool without Taylor's word — it lands
                               # on "strong, silent" in `leads week`. Recorded as pipeline events; the DM
                               # ones print, the email ones are `outreach send --touch 3|10`

  leads kit                    # Saturday's six counters, faults and the opener (one page)
  leads kit --for 2026-10-04   # a different Saturday
  leads kit --last             # reprint the last kit without touching Google
  leads kit --census-only      # no Places calls: what the census alone knows
  leads candidates [--n 20]    # the ranked pool the kit picks from (no spend)
  leads kit --remote           # today's six ready-to-send messages (ROADMAP B25): DM, email, faults
  leads kit --remote --previews # the same, with a preview site built for every pick (B45)
  leads diagnose "Name[, City]" [--group "Utah Small Business Owners"]
                               # three lines to paste under a group post, and the lead logged
  leads preview "Name, City"   # that lead's own website, filled from the census row (B45)
  leads preview --kit          # one for each of today's remote-kit picks
  leads preview ls             # every preview, how long it has left
  leads preview sweep          # the expired ones come down (LEADS_NOW moves the clock)
  leads preview --remove NAME  # a takedown, now
  leads preview --claim NAME --slug mikes-pool-care   # client new + site new from the same files
  leads batch --segment services [--category plumber] [--city Lehi] [--n 50] [--json]
                               # the email lane's batch (B90): one trade across the corridor, each with its address
                               # and two true specifics, a fault first; held 56 days once printed. --stats sizes it,
                               # --last reprints, --live reads a listing one fault short (capped a day)
  leads preview --place PLACE_ID --json   # one business's preview as one JSON object with its url (B90)
  leads preview --from-press HASH --json  # a press on a letter's link: build or reuse, the brief on a first press (B91)
  leads preview --press-tokens --json     # the links the see page may answer for, active or removed (B91)
  leads doctor

Preview sites (B45, plan ~/projects/plans/19-preview-sites.md): the segment's
template filled from the listing alone — name, category → the services that
category implies (templates/previews/categories.json, one row per category in
client-leads/scripts/services.json), phone, city, hours, "5.0★ on Google, 88
reviews" linking to the listing, one stock photo. Never their Google photos,
never the text of a review, never a street address, never a price. All of them
live in one Cloudflare Pages project at previews.patchlamp.com/<slug>/, noindex
twice over (a robots meta and X-Robots-Tag from the project's _headers), with
the footer that says what the page is and a 30-day expiry. Deterministic: no
model call, so six previews cost $0.

Segments (B44, VISION § Decided 2026-09-28: services first, restaurants one of five):
  kit, kit --remote, candidates and next read the services census (B43's
  `businesses` table in the same wasatch.db) by default once it holds a kit's
  worth (six service businesses with a phone and no site of their own); until
  then, and with --segment restaurant, everything below is the restaurant census
  exactly as before. diagnose looks a name up in both.
  --segment services|creatives|retail|nonprofit|restaurant|all   (LEADS_SEGMENT sets the default)
  leads kit --segment services  # the six nearest American Fork with no site of their own (a call list, not
                                # Saturday counters): presence class, the faults, the opener, the close, the ladder
  leads kit --remote --segment creatives   # six messages greeted by the business (or the first name in it)
  leads diagnose "Name, City"   # a name in the services census answers from the census, no Places call
                                # (--live reads the listing too); an unknown name is still looked up live
  The pool for a non-restaurant segment: presence none, page (Facebook, Instagram,
  Linktree…), directory (Thumbtack, Angi…), dead (business.site, a link that
  doesn't load) or builder (a free Wix/GoDaddy/Square… address); `own` sites are
  left out, `unknown` is read from the website link without a fetch.

The pick: marketplace-only independents from the census
(client-leads/wasatch.db: on DoorDash/Uber/Grubhub with no ordering
of their own), operational, with a phone, at least --min-reviews reviews,
nearest to home first, skipping anyone kitted in the last eight weeks. Each
candidate's Google listing is read through Place Details (Places API New) until
six are open Saturday by 11:30 (hours unknown counts, flagged). The page lists
them in visiting order from home with what is wrong on the listing (no hours,
closed Saturdays, few photos, no website or a marketplace link for one, a low
recent review, a stale listing), then the counter opener.

Money: one Place Details call per candidate, cached seven days under
~/.local/state/claude-tools/leads/details/, roughly $0.025 each at the
Enterprise + Atmosphere SKU; each run appends one line to the toolbelt ledger
(~/.local/state/claude-tools/ledger.jsonl) with the calls it made. Owner
replies to reviews are not in the Places API, so "unanswered" is not claimed;
that arrives with the Business Profile connection (B11/B12).

The tool line (B40, plan ~/projects/plans/15-web-tools.md § How we sell it,
point 3): a counter whose listing shows no way to book online (Google's
`reservable` is unset and the website isn't on a booking host, BOOKING_HOSTS)
is marked "No booking link" and the page ends with the tool line, which
points at patchlamp.com/tools. In the remote kit, a service business
(SERVICE_TYPES / SERVICE_SUFFIXES; the census is food, so it is rare there)
with no booking link gets the second message, `tool_dm_text`. Neither names
a price or offers ordering.

Config, by name, never printed:
  GOOGLE_MAPS_API_KEY   ~/.config/claude-tools/env (setenv.sh). Without it the
                        kit is census-only and says so on its first line.
  LEADS_DB              the census (default client-leads/wasatch.db)
  LEADS_HOME            "lat,lng" of home (default American Fork)
  LEADS_STATE           state dir (default ~/.local/state/claude-tools/leads)
  LEADS_MAIL_ADDRESS    the postal address a cold email must carry (CAN-SPAM);
                        not a secret, kept in the toolbelt env beside the keys.
                        Without it every email draft says it isn't ready to send.
  LEADS_GROUPS_LOG      the human-readable log of remote and group-thread leads
                        (default ~/projects/social/leads-from-groups.md)
  LEADS_PREVIEWS        the previews' state: site/ (what is uploaded) and
                        meta/<slug>.json (never uploaded). Default
                        ~/.local/state/claude-tools/previews
  LEADS_PREVIEW_PROJECT the Pages project they all live in (patchlamp-previews)
  LEADS_PREVIEW_HOST    the host to build links from, when it isn't the one the
                        last publish reported (tests)
  LEADS_PREVIEW_YES     =1 passes `site previews --yes`, which is what lets the
                        very first publish create the Pages project. Until
                        Taylor gives that word, a publish stops and says so
                        (GROWTH § 10, TAYLOR-TODO §1 "Preview sites").
  LEADS_NOW             an ISO date standing in for today: the previews' expiry, and the
                        clock `today`, `cadence`, `brief` and `week` read (so a day-10
                        touch is provable without waiting ten days). Unset in normal use.
  LEADS_KIT_PREVIEWS    `leads today` builds a preview for every pick it makes (B45) by default once the
                        previews project is published (project.json has a pages_host); =0 turns it
                        off, =1 forces it on. Never with --no-save.
  LEADS_BOOKING_URL     the booking link `leads brief` ends on (Cal.com); shared with `outreach`
  OUTREACH_STATE        read-only here: `leads today` reads the email lane's replies.jsonl for
                        "yesterday's replies", and never writes anything under it
  LEADS_LIVE_READS_PER_DAY  listing reads `leads batch --live` may make a day (default 100, ~$0.025 each)
  LEADS_CLIENTS_DIR     the client workspaces whose addresses, domains and phones a batch keeps out (~/projects/clients)
  LEADS_OUTREACH_BIN    the `outreach` a batch asks for the suppression list (beside this file)
  LEADS_PAGE_CHECK      =0: a batch doesn't re-read a pick's page, so an old copyright year is never said
                        (nor a broken link, a broken image or a failing secure address: those are asked again too);
                        LEADS_PAGE_FIXTURE a JSON {url: html}, LEADS_STATUS_FIXTURE a JSON {url: status} (tests)
  LEADS_PIPELINE        the pipeline, one event per line (default
                        ~/projects/private-docs/leads/pipeline.jsonl: backed up
                        nightly, in no repo — it holds names and numbers). The
                        census stays read-only; nothing here writes to it.

The remote lane (B25, plan ~/projects/plans/09-social-strategy.md § Facebook
groups): same census and diagnostic, delivered as messages instead of
addresses. The census holds no owner names or email addresses; what it does
hold is each place's top search results, which is where an Instagram handle
or a Facebook page is found. Leads with one are picked first, and the draft
says which channel to use. Owner names are not claimed.

The kit's machine-readable seam (`leads kit --remote --json`), which
`bin/outreach` (B46) reads. Add keys; never rename one:

  {"date": "2026-09-28", "segment": "services",
   "picks": [{"place_id", "name", "first" (the first name the business carries,
              else the business), "category", "segment", "city", "phone",
              "email"|null, "instagram" (handle)|null, "facebook" (url)|null,
              "faults": [str], "preview_url"|null, "maps_url",
              "message" (the DM draft) and "summary" beyond the agreed shape,
              B104: "email_unconfirmed" {address, why, confidence}|null and
              "reach_unconfirmed" [{field, value, confidence, why, label, profile}]}]}

Is it their place? (B104/B107, plan ~/projects/plans/44-wrong-business-handles.md.) The
`reach` table's columns hold only a handle or an address client-leads/scripts/reach.py tied
to the place (`high`); the rest sit in its `evidence` with a confidence and a reason and are
named in `unconfirmed`. The readers here use `high` only: `email`, `instagram`, `facebook`
above are never anything else. A `low` one is said as "Instagram: unconfirmed, call-only
(why)", an `unsure` one (research doubted it) as "Instagram @x: unconfirmed, look before
sending (why)" with its profile link and never as the DM line, a `rejected` one as
"Instagram refused (why)". A column value from before B104 (no confidence) reads as `low`
until `reach.py --check` has run over it. `leads show` and `brief` say a logged handle that
isn't high instead of printing it (the pipeline is never rewritten), `leads batch` writes to
a `high` address only (`emails.confidence`), and `leads recheck` runs `reach.py --check`
over the week's messaged leads. LEADS_REACH_PY points at the reach script (default
scripts/reach.py beside the census); `doctor` says where it is.

`leads kit --json` without --remote is unchanged: the picks as a plain list. Every
remote run also saves that envelope beside its page (state/remote/<date>[-segment].json),
which is where `leads today` reads the morning's six from instead of paying twice.

Hosts (B71, `client-leads/scripts/hosts.py`, plan ~/projects/plans/32-who-hosts-it.md): when the
census has a `hosts` table (place_id, vendor, evidence, status, checked, url, kind) the candidate
and kit lines carry `hibu ($449+/mo, 404)` — whose platform the site is on, that vendor's public
monthly band from client-leads/vendor_prices.md (LEADS_VENDOR_PRICES overrides the path), and
whether it answers. `candidates --paying` puts an agency-hosted dead or parked site first; `brief`
prints one sentence in the vendor's own public price; the remote kit's JSON gains `paying` (the
letter's `{paying}` line, null when the vendor is unknown, free or unpriced) and `host`. Never a
guess at the business's own bill: every sentence is about the vendor. A missing table means no
fingerprint yet, and nothing changes. Nothing here writes to it.

Language (B74, `client-leads/scripts/language.py`): when the census has a `language` table
(place_id, language, evidence, checked, basis) a row that speaks Spanish to its customers carries a tag
on its kit, `today` and `candidates` line — `lang: es`, `lang: es (name only)` when the name is all
there was to read, `lang: es+en` for both; English and unknown rows carry nothing. `brief` prints the
evidence in one line and the remote kit's JSON gains `language` ({language, basis, why, checked} or
null) — the seam the Spanish pitch will read. A missing table means no pass yet, and nothing changes.

Reach (B61, `client-leads/scripts/reach.py`): when the census has a `reach` table
(place_id, instagram, facebook, email, source, checked, evidence) the kit's picks take
a handle or an address from it *after* the census's own columns — the listing's own
link and, for a restaurant, its search results, win. `leads doctor` prints the coverage,
or says the table isn't there yet. Nothing here writes to it.

The pipeline's event shape (one JSON object a line; fields are added, never renamed):
  ts date key place_id name city outcome stage next note who email phone via reach
  channel  where a messaged/talked touch went (facebook instagram email text call form, B116):
           required on `messaged`; a line without one reads "channel not recorded", never a guess.
           On a `touch_due` event it is the planned channel (dm email call). `channel_by` is "kit" when
           `leads sent` took it from the kit (planned, not witnessed), "backfill WHO DATE" for `leads channel`.
  source   the channel (email dm group saturday referral inbound mail), so `week --by
           channel` can cut the funnel; `--source` sets it, else it follows --via, the
           channel the lead is already on, or the reach the kit used
  was      the faults named in the first message, so the day-30 read can say what changed
  next_by  "hand" when Taylor named the date (`--next thu`): the cadence never writes over it
  kind     "touch_due" for a cadence event, with `touch` (3|10|30|45|60|90) and `channel`;
           "strength" for Taylor's override (`leads strength`): never a lead by itself, and it always wins
  strength strong | good | weak as scored when the event was written (B73), and `reasons` the keys behind it
           (client-leads/strength.md's table); `week --by strength` reads the first message's

Strength (B73, plan ~/projects/plans/33-leads-by-strength.md): every candidate and lead is strong, good or weak
from named reasons — an agency-hosted dead site (the strongest), a dead link of their own, no website, a listing
that embarrasses them, 10–300 reviews at 4.3★+, within 10 miles, a reach with evidence, a named owner, a trade
that quotes jobs; against: a chain, a franchise, a live builder site under $50, a rating under 4.0. The weights
and the thresholds are client-leads/strength.md's tables (LEADS_STRENGTH overrides the path; the defaults are
in STRENGTH_REASONS). Candidates, the kits and `leads today` put strong first and say why on every line.

positional arguments:
  {kit,diagnose,candidates,log,next,sent,channel,replies,due,recheck,today,brief,cadence,strength,show,week,pipeline,preview,batch,doctor}
    kit                 Saturday's counters, one page
    diagnose            three lines on a business's Google listing, for a
                        group thread
    candidates          the pool the kit picks from (no spend)
    log                 log a conversation: leads log "Name[, City]" OUTCOME
                        [note...]
    next                the day's list: follow-ups due, then new leads
                        (default tomorrow)
    sent                picks from the last remote kit that went out: leads
                        sent 1 3 4 | all
    channel             backfill: the channel of a messaged/talked line logged
                        without one (B116)
    replies             how often the owner answers Google reviews, as a
                        person read it (B116)
    due                 follow-ups due today
    recheck             the week's messaged leads: each logged handle or
                        address judged again against the place (B104, reach.py
                        --check through LEADS_REACH_PY; $0)
    today               the 07:30 message: the six, yesterday's replies,
                        what's due, the first call
    brief               one screen before a call: the fault, the preview, the
                        history, the objection, the close
    cadence             the touches a silent lead is owed by its strength (§
                        5.5): weak 3/10, good 3/10/30, strong 3/10/30/45/60/90
    strength            a lead's strength and why; `strength NAME
                        strong|good|weak "why"` is your word
    show                one lead's history
    week                this week's numbers
    pipeline            every lead by stage
    preview             a lead's own website, built from the census row (B45):
                        NAME | --kit | ls | sweep
    batch               the email lane's batch (B90): fifty or fewer in one
                        trade, each with its address and two true specifics (a
                        fault first); --stats sizes the lane

options:
  -h, --help            show this help message and exit
--- stderr
--- exit 0
